Download and read public benchmark datasets

Source: R/graph-datasets.R
download-datasets.Rd

These functions download data only when called, from the original sources, into root, and check the archive's MD5 checksum when one is known. Nothing is downloaded during package checks and no dataset is redistributed with the package; check each source's terms of use before redistributing the data.

Usage

download_tu_dataset(name, root = tempdir(), md5 = NULL, overwrite = FALSE)

read_tu_dataset(dir, name = basename(dir))

download_planetoid_raw(
  name = c("cora", "citeseer"),
  root = tempdir(),
  md5 = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE
)

read_linqs_citation(dir, name = basename(dir))

Arguments

name

Dataset name.

root

Directory to store downloads.

md5

Expected archive checksum; NULL uses the recorded value for known datasets and skips the check otherwise.

overwrite

Download again even if the archive exists.

dir

Directory with the extracted files.

Value

download_tu_dataset() returns a graph_dataset; download_planetoid_raw() returns a graph_data.

Details

  • download_tu_dataset(): TU Dortmund graph kernel benchmarks (Morris et al. 2020), for example "MUTAG" and "PROTEINS", from https://www.chrsmrrs.com/graphkerneldatasets/.

  • download_planetoid_raw(): the original LINQS releases of Cora and CiteSeer (Sen et al. 2008) from https://linqs-data.soe.ucsc.edu/. These are the raw citation graphs. They are not the Planetoid splits used by Kipf and Welling (2017) and PyG's Planetoid class (which also drop and reorder nodes), so results are not comparable to published leaderboards. Open Graph Benchmark datasets are not yet supported.

read_tu_dataset() and read_linqs_citation() parse already downloaded files.

In the LINQS .cites files each line is cited citing. The returned graph is directed from the citing paper to the cited paper. Citations to papers missing from .content are dropped and counted in metadata$dropped_edges.
